# YM26: 北远山村 Beiyuan Shancun, "Village of the Distant Northern Mountains"

Malone calls it Pei Yuan Shan T'sun.

Wave 2 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM26` · Page: `/scenes/#YM26` · Row: `research/buildings/YM26-beiyuan-shancun/`

## What it was

北远山村 Beiyuan Shancun, an imitation farm village on both banks of the river east of 鱼跃鸢飞, among fields: at the west end of the stone-walled north bank 兰野 Lanye, behind it 绘雨精舍, south-west 水村图, then a pair of linked storeyed halls, 皆春阁 Jiechun Ge in front and 稻凉楼 Daoliang Lou behind, further west 涉趣楼 and 湛虚书屋 (S05 j82:5a). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).

From the inventory row: **built** by 1742 (first dated item); **changed** 课农轩 rebuilt 1817 as a hall of 5 bays, 2 rolls, front annex; **destroyed** 课农轩, 观音庵 and service rooms survived 1860; lost around 1900 (S05, S02, S08, S01, S360, S361).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Preface of 1744: "循苑牆度北闗村落鱗次竹籬茅舎巷陌交通" (S05 j82:5b): along the garden wall past the north gate, a village of thatched huts with bamboo fences and lanes, herdsmen's flutes and fishermen's songs answering the pestles; the poem lists water-wheels on the banks and a herd-boy on a buffalo.

### How later sources differ

Major change after 1744: in 1817 (Jiaqing) the five-bay 课农轩 Kenong Xuan with a three-bay annex was built on the sites of 皆春阁, 稻凉楼, 涉趣楼 and 湛虚书屋 (E1756, S361); so for 1860 the west part of 北远山村 is 课农轩 (YM51), not the linked towers of S05. Some buildings survived 1860 under guard, say the editors (E1756).

## Interior and setting

### Interior

Nothing written yet.

### The garden around it

Thatched cottages, bamboo fences, water-wheels on the banks, seedling boats in the paddies (S05 j82:5b-6a); a stone revetment on the north bank (北岸石垣, S05 j82:5a).

- **Q59. Twin claims to hold loosely.** 海晏堂 follows the Grand Trianon: Beurdeley 1971 p.68, repeated widely; Rabreau (S415 p.81) says its grounds would be sought in vain.
